TL;DR
You're a communications professional who can plan and execute the work that advances Lovable's objectives across EU and Swedish policy environments, making sure our voice is heard on the issues that matter most. You'll pair sharp corporate communications with real policy fluency — working closely with internal teams and external partners to help policymakers, media, and other stakeholders understand Lovable's perspective on the key files and issues that shape the environment we operate in.
This is a balanced role, equal parts policy operator and corporate communicator. You'll report to the European Communications and Public Affairs Lead.
Why Lovable?
Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.
We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.
Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.
What you'll do
This role makes sure Lovable has a credible, constructive voice in the rooms that matter — building a presence worth listening to and developing clear positions that reflect what Lovable actually builds and believes.
Advocate Lovable's positions on key policy files. You'll build and run our engagement with policy representatives across EU and Swedish institutions.
Own corporate communications on policy issues. Statements, briefings, op-eds, speaking moments, and the proactive announcements that build credibility over time. You'll develop the strategy, write the materials, manage media relationships, and make sure each piece reinforces the others.
Track the regulatory agenda and turn it into a point of view. You'll monitor the files that affect us and develop clear positions that reflect the company's reality and ambitions.
Build coalitions and work through industry. You'll represent Lovable in trade associations and industry groups, finding shared causes that move issues forward.
Act as a comms and policy partner to our cross-functional team. You'll work closely with the communications and cross-functional teams in preparing for engagements with policymakers, institutions, and press, strengthening the company’s voice in the European AI debate.
Who you are
You've operated in and around the policy world. That might mean an EU institution, a trade association, a think tank, or a public affairs firm. Wherever you've been, you know how a file moves from idea to law, and you can read the politics, formal and informal, that determine what actually happens.
You understand policy and can communicate it. You have experience from both policy work and corporate communications, and you're equally comfortable speaking to policymakers and media alike.
You can drive an issue forward in a complex political environment. You're comfortable with ambiguity and competing agendas, and you know how to prioritize when everything feels urgent.
You're a sharp writer with editorial judgment. You can turn a dense regulatory development into a crisp briefing, opinion piece or clean position statement.
You connect dots that other people don't see. You look at a piece of draft legislation and think ahead on what it means for the industry as well as what Lovable should say and to whom.
You're a genuine cross-functional collaborator. You work easily with cross-functional stakeholders, external partners, and coalitions. You don't wait to be invited into the room. You're not precious about who gets credit. You just make things work.
You're deeply curious about AI, technology policy, and the industry landscape. You keep up with what happens in the world instinctively — the news, the regulatory moves, the debates as they unfold. You understand where the conversation is heading well enough to spot a risk or an opportunity before someone hands it to you.
What you need to know
This is not a role where you set the strategy and hand off execution. You'll be writing the first drafts of our position statements, building the relationships and showing up in the room as a Lovable representative.
We move fast and plans change. The job runs on two clocks at once: you'll react to the urgent issue that lands today while building the relationships and positions that set us up for success in the long term. If you need a settled environment with predictable workflows, this will be frustrating. If you find that kind of pace energizing, you'll love it.
We're building public affairs and communications at a company that is itself being built. That means you'll have real influence over how this function develops in Europe: the positions, the relationships, the standards. That's the upside of being early.
Finally: joining Lovable Comms means you're deeply curious, data-driven, and not extremely precious about role boundaries. You find ways to work smarter with AI, to measure what matters, and to step into work that isn't technically "yours" when the moment calls for it.
About your application
Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.
We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

Mycronic is a global high-tech company whose innovative solutions have been advancing electronics technology for over 40 years. Today we continue to grow and serve customers in an expanding variety of industries. What we do impacts the future of technology, and in turn, the way we live our lives tomorrow. We’re looking for people to join our talented, motivated and friendly team on the cutting-edge. Here, in an open, collaborative and flexible environment, you’ll work alongside leading industry experts and take on challenging projects that bring tomorrow’s electronics to life. If you have several years of work experience within software development and embedded systems and wants to be part of a growing company with world leading products, this is for you!
About the role
Mycronic has experienced strong growth in recent years, both organically and through acquisitions. With headquarters in Sweden, Mycronic is a global organization with subsidiaries, agents, and distributors in over 50 countries. Mycronic is divided into four divisions, and in this role, you will belong to PCB Assembly Solutions (PA). PA is a leading provider of equipment and solutions for surface mount technology (SMT) to electronics manufacturers who require rapid production adjustments while maintaining high efficiency. PA delivers systems for circuit board assembly, including both complete line solutions and individual systems for specific process steps, as well as advanced software for assembly process management and connected factories. In this role, you will be part of a team of 7 team members and collaborate with several functions across the company, such as architects, project managers and other software teams within for example AI.
You are offered
The opportunity to work in a multi-cultural company with knowledgeable, friendly and goal-oriented colleagues.
To work in an exciting company in a growth phase, where you can make a real impact in a fun and dynamic environment. Mycronic is a global company, yet small enough for you to truly make a difference.
The opportunity to work with world-leading products. The future of electronics production is increasingly complex. Denser boards, a wider range of miniaturized components, more NPIs and erratic production schedules. To address these challenges Mycronic has developed the industry’s fastest, most flexible and most precise jet printing and solder paste dispensing systems. Mycronic jet printing technology makes it possible to dispense solder paste for the most challenging circuit boards and components, with micrometer accuracy, maximum speed and perfect quality solder joints. Read more here: https://www.mycronic.com/product-areas/pcb-assembly/products/smt/jet-printing/.
Mycronic has a large software organization which will provide you with optimal opportunities to develop your knowledge in various areas of computer science – such as software architecture for robotics, machine learning, AI, optimization, and computer vision.

Work tasks
You will work in a broad developer role where you will truly have the opportunity to influence the final solution of the products. The Mycronic Jet Printer, which is the product area you will be developing the software for, includes electronics, mechanics, and software, creating exciting opportunities for those who want to work with complex software development involving multiple technical disciplines. We are continuously working to enhance our products; user-friendliness, particularly in terms of automation and user interfaces, which will also be part of your development work. Your primary focus will be on improving the products, with opportunities to contribute your ideas and collaborate as a team to create the best solutions. This may involve anything from adding capability features and reducing energy consumption to updating the GUI. Mycronic has both R&D, lab, and production in-house, meaning you will work close to the products you develop, which also gives you the opportunity to see the "real world" results of your work.
We are looking for
This is a role for someone with a strong background in software development and an interest in understanding the entire product and an ambition to grow into a software architect role. As a software developer you will have a key role in the product development since this is where all the technology in the machine comes together to provide the system functionality that meets the user. You will be involved in everything from requirements gathering to design, architecture and development and collaborate with several stakeholders. As a person, we see it as particularly important that you are goal- and detail-oriented and have strong collaboration skills. You also have a will to contribute with your ideas, and just like your colleagues, you always strive to develop yourself and contribute to the team´s collective growth. We expect you to make a strong contribution by adding new functionality, maintaining high quality and by helping to introduce new technology and processes to increase team efficiency.
You likely have:
A bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, electronics, mechatronics, or a similar field.
Strong software development experience with the capability and ambition to take on broader architectural responsibilities in a few years.
Knowledge in Java.
Strong knowledge of software development in Linux.
Experience of working with software systems that interact with embedded software and hardware.
Strong knowledge in English and good knowledge in Swedish (or have the desire to learn)

It is considered advantageous if you have: 
Knowledge in C and/or C++

AI is changing not only what software we build, but how we build it. As our HiveAI Engineering Manager, you will lead the team at the centre of that shift. You will combine people leadership, strong engineering judgement and AI-assisted development to turn ideas into production-ready products faster.
This is an opportunity to help shape both a product and the way of working around it. You will build and lead a small, high-trust development team where AI accelerates engineering without compromising quality, security or maintainability.
About the role
As Engineering Manager for HiveAI, you lead the people and shape how the team works and delivers. You will lead an international team with developers based across several Fellowmind countries, so building trust, alignment and a strong team culture across locations will be an important part of your leadership.
You will work as a peer alongside our Product Manager and Chief Architect, each with a clear but closely connected area of ownership. The Product Manager drives the why and what. The Chief Architect sets the technical direction and guardrails. You lead the team and create the conditions for great engineering.
The way we build matters. The HiveAI team works from problems and hypotheses, using AI to move quickly from idea to experiment and prototype. What proves valuable is then hardened into secure, scalable and maintainable software. You will help define what this way of working looks like in practice as the team grows.
You will lead a team that brings together platform developers, who build and maintain HiveAI itself, and Frontier Fellows (Forward Deployed Engineers), who work close to our implementation teams and customers and bring what they learn and build back into the product. Your job is to bring these two perspectives together as one engineering team.
What you will do:
Build and lead the team. Own hiring, 1:1s, development and performance conversations, and build a strong, high-trust engineering culture across a distributed international team.
Design the way we deliver. Drive fast build-and-learn cycles, remove impediments and favour working demos and clear ship, change or stop decisions.
Turn prototypes into products. Together with the Chief Architect, make sure promising experiments cross the line into production with the engineering quality they need.
Make AI a real engineering capability. Coach developers in prompting, coding agents, AI-assisted testing and code review, and continuously evolve how the team works with AI.
Protect engineering understanding. AI should make engineers faster and help them learn, not become a substitute for understanding the systems they build.
Keep the focus on outcomes. Build a team that makes good decisions about what to build, how to build it and when AI is, and is not, the right tool.

Who are you?
You are a people leader who still thinks like an engineer.
You probably spent a significant part of your career as a software developer before moving into technical and people leadership. Today, you might be an Engineering Manager, Software Development Manager or a Tech Lead with people responsibility, ideally in a SaaS or software product company.
You are comfortable when the destination is clearer than the route to get there. You coach and enable your team, make good decisions with incomplete information and know when a fast prototype is good enough to learn from, but not good enough to ship.
We believe that you bring:
Extensive professional experience in software development, followed by at least 2–3 years of people leadership, either as an Engineering Manager or as a Tech Lead with direct people responsibility.
Hands-on experience using AI coding tools and agents, such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code or similar, as part of real software development.
Strong engineering practices across CI/CD, automated testing, code review and secure development.
Experience from a SaaS or software product environment, where teams own what they build beyond the first release.
Experience leading distributed or international teams, with the ability to coach, communicate and build a strong team culture across locations, mainly through digital ways of working.
Experience with Azure and the Microsoft technology stack, which is highly valuable given HiveAI's technology landscape.
The ability to start from a problem statement and a hypothesis, and to shape the route to a solution together with the team as you learn.
Professional proficiency in English and the local language of the country in which you are applying: Swedish, Danish or Dutch.

You do not need to be the person writing the most code in the team. What matters is your technical background. It gives you the credibility and judgement to coach great engineers and challenge decisions. It also lets you create an environment where they can move exceptionally fast without losing control of what they build.
What is HiveAI?
At Fellowmind, we're building HiveAI, a platform for developing, deploying and operating AI solutions at scale. It provides a secure and scalable foundation for enterprise AI and enables organisations to move beyond isolated experiments towards AI solutions that become part of how the business actually operates.
At its core is the HiveAI Technology, built on Microsoft Azure, which provides the foundation for deploying, scaling and managing AI agents securely. Around it sits the HiveAI Agent Lifecycle, helping organisations develop, deploy, manage and continuously improve their AI agents over time.
Why Fellowmind?
You will join HiveAI at a stage where there is still plenty to shape. You will have real influence on how the team, the product and the way of working take form, with an international organisation and the Microsoft ecosystem behind you.
Fellowmind combines deep industry knowledge and personal guidance with Microsoft cloud technology across ERP, cloud infrastructure, data & AI, CRM, intranet and Modern Workplace. We are an international organisation with more than 2,000 colleagues across Europe.
Our culture is built around putting people at the heart of what we do. We value collaboration, personal responsibility, development and the freedom to find a sustainable balance between work and life.

Why Lovable?
Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.
We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.
Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.
What this role is and what it isn’t
It is a senior are lead role with scope. You’ll run an organization that spans product, platform, and applied AI - with other managers, senior engineers, and AI agents reporting in - and you’ll be accountable for what that organization ships, how it operates, and the business outcomes it drives.
It is still close enough to the work that you can drop into a Tech Lead role on a hard problem when the situation demands it. We don’t measure leadership IC time as a percentage. We measure it as the ability to pick up the work and ship at the bar you’re asking of your team.
It isn’t a role for managers who think of themselves as engineering-adjacent. You need to be credible in code, design, and on-call - and you need to want to be.
It isn’t a role for leaders who only think about engineering. We expect you to reason end-to-end about the business - economics, product, GTM, customers - and to make calls that are best for the company, not just best for your team.

What we’re looking for
15+ years of engineering experience, including 6+ years of people management at a pre-IPO startup, scale-up or frontier tech company, and at least 2 years of managing managers. Strong IC track record before management.
You’ve run an engineering organization of 30+ with managers and senior engineers reporting in. You can speak concretely about how you structured the org, how you hired up to that scale, and what you’d do differently.
Still hands-on at the Tech Lead level: you can pick up an unfamiliar codebase, design and ship a non-trivial change, run an incident, and review code at a high bar. You haven’t let your engineering muscle atrophy.
You’ve thought hard about humans and AI agents on the same team. What humans should and shouldn’t delegate. How productivity gets measured when the unit of work is shifting. Strong opinions, lightly held.
Comfortable navigating ambiguity and driving clarity at an organisational level, not just technically. You write the doc that aligns three teams instead of waiting for someone else to.
Deep technical credibility in at least one area - full-stack product (React/TypeScript + Go/Rust), platform and developer experience (Kubernetes, sandboxing, observability, CI/CD, application frameworks), or applied AI (training, evals, agent systems, model serving).
Cross-functional to your core and business-fluent: you work seamlessly across design, product, and go-to-market, and know how to bring people along with you; andable to reason end-to-end about unit economics, product strategy, GTM, and customer outcomes
Track record of building and growing teams: you’ve hired senior engineers others wanted to work with, grown managers under you who became great in their own right, and set up career growth and performance practices that didn’t require constant maintenance. People follow you between companies.
Based in Stockholm or London or ready to relocate — this is an on-site, 5-days-a-week role.

What you’ll do
In one sentence: Run the engineering organization that builds Lovable - humans and agents both - and stay close enough to the work to be the senior engineer in the room when it matters.
Lead engineering. Product, platform, and applied AI under one roof. Own the roadmap and the business outcomes the org is on the hook for.
Set technical direction across the org: drive the design docs and architectural decisions that span teams, push back hard on weak plans (including your own), and hold a high bar for what ships.
Shape engineering culture: how we ship, how we write code, how we hire, how we deploy agents. Set norms that outlast any single project.
Ship fast: at Lovable the question is always “how fast can we get this to users?” You bias toward production and pull research, prototypes, and experiments into reality on the order of days and weeks, not quarters.
Build the operating model for an engineering org where humans and AI agents work side by side. We’re inventing this in public, and you’ll set the patterns the rest of the company learns from.
Operate as a peer to the executive team. Own outcomes that span beyond engineering, make the company’s biggest calls alongside the rest of leadership, and translate them back into engineering work that matters.

Our tech stack
We’re building with tools that both humans and AI love:
Frontend: React, TypeScript
Backend: Go and Rust
Cloud: Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, many LLM providers
Data: ClickHouse, Firestore, Spanner, BigQuery
DevOps & tooling: Kubernetes, gVisor-based sandboxing for agentic workloads, GitHub Actions, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Terraform
Local tooling: Nix, DevEnv

About your application
Please submit your application in English — it’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.
We treat all candidates equally — if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

 Ready to join us?
Help us unlock human creativity and build the future of software creation.

jobs.employer_name: H & M Hennes & Mauritz GBC AB
jobs.description:
Job Description

As Unit Manager for Cyber Risk & Assurance, you will lead H&M Group’s capabilities for cyber risk management, governance, compliance and assurance, playing a key role in strengthening the organisation’s security, resilience and ability to manage cyber risk in line with its risk appetite and regulatory obligations. 
As a member of the Cyber Security Leadership Team reporting to the CISO, you will share accountability for the overall cyber security strategy, priorities and long-term development of the Cyber Security function. Working closely with leaders across business, technology and cyber security, you will help shape outcomes that balance business objectives, security needs and risk management across H&M Group. 
You will provide strategic leadership for H&M Group’s Cyber Risk & Assurance capability, bringing together Cyber Security Frameworks, Supply Chain Security Risk and Security Control Assurance. Through your leadership, you will drive the continued evolution of cyber risk management and control assurance. 
WHAT YOU WILL DO
Lead the strategic direction, maturity and long-term development of H&M Group’s Cyber, Risk & Assurance capability, defining and evolving the strategy, roadmap and operating model in alignment with business, technology and cyber security objectives. 
Contribute as a member of the Cyber Security Leadership Team to the overall cyber security strategy, priorities and long-term capability development. 
Drive the continued development and maturity of the Information Security Management System (ISMS), including frameworks, policies and governance structures that enable consistent and effective management of cyber risk across H&M Group. 
Provide oversight and assurance of cyber security risks and controls, promoting transparency, accountability and effective risk-based decision-making. 
Strengthen H&M Group’s approach to security policy and compliance, regulatory requirements, security control assurance and governance reporting. 
Drive the continued development of third-party and supply chain security risk management, ensuring risks are identified, assessed and managed through effective governance and oversight. 
Lead budgeting, resource and investment planning, vendor strategy and prioritisation to support Cyber Risk & Assurance and wider cyber security objectives. 
Foster a high-performing, collaborative and inclusive culture focused on strong accountability, continuous improvement and business value. 

Leadership as a Unit Manager  
As a Unit Manager and member of the Cyber Security Leadership Team, you provide strategic leadership for your unit while contributing to the overall direction and development of the Cyber Security function. You develop high-performing leadership teams, drive organisational effectiveness and capability development. You demonstrate enterprise leadership by collaborating across the business, influencing senior stakeholders and supporting decisions that create value beyond your own unit. 
WHO YOU ARE
We are looking for someone with: 
8+ years of people management experience in cyber security, technology risk, governance, compliance, assurance or a closely related field. 
Proven experience leading enterprise-scale cyber risk, governance, compliance or assurance capabilities in a complex global organisation. 
Proven experience leading through managers and developing high-performing leadership teams, with accountability for a multidisciplinary organisation and its outcomes. 
Experience as a member of a senior cyber security, technology, risk or enterprise leadership team, contributing to shared strategy, priorities, investment decisions and organisational outcomes beyond your own area of responsibility. 
Strong knowledge of cyber security risk management, governance, compliance and assurance principles, methodologies and operating models. 
Strong knowledge of security frameworks, policies, standards and controls, and experience translating regulatory and internal requirements into effective security governance. 
Strong understanding of third-party and supply chain security risk management in complex global environments. 
Experience establishing meaningful cyber risk, governance and assurance metrics and translating risk and control information into clear business implications, priorities and decisions. 
Experience managing significant budgets, investments, resources, sourcing arrangements and external partners, including strategic vendor relationships. 
Excellent communication and influencing skills, with proven experience engaging senior and executive stakeholders and communicating complex cyber risk, regulatory and assurance topics in a clear and pragmatic way. 
Sound judgement and decision-making capability in complex, uncertain and risk-sensitive situations. 

 

Additional Information

This is a fulltime permanent role based in Stockholm, Sweden. 
If you believe your experience, skills, and ambitions align with this role, please submit your CV in English.
Diversity, Inclusion, and Innovation 
At H&M Group, we're deeply committed to fostering a Diverse & Inclusive environment. We actively seek out qualified candidates regardless of race, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, national origin, disability, or age. 
Our commitment to an inclusive workplace drives our dynamic and forward-thinking culture. Regardless of your background, origin, or preferences, your application is warmly welcomed. We value diverse perspectives and skills, and every applicant contributes to our vibrant, creative community. Join us and be part of the future we're building. 
Our Offer 
At H&M Group, you're not just joining a team – you're joining a value-driven culture and an expansive tech network. Enjoy perks like staff discount cards, flexible work arrangements, wellness benefits, parental support, and more. Here, you're encouraged to be yourself, experiment, and chart your own growth path. As you flourish, so do we, with opportunities to create tangible impacts and shape the future. 
WHO WE ARE​ 
H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices, and sustainable solutions. We want to liberate fashion for the many, and our customers are at the heart of every decision we make.​ 
​We are made up of thousands of passionate and talented colleagues united by our shared culture and values. Together, we want to use our power, our scale, and our knowledge to push the fashion industry towards a more inclusive and sustainable future. ​ 
​WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE ​ 
We offer all our employees at H&M Group attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe. All our employees receive a staff discount card, usable on all our H&M Group brands in stores and online. Brands covered by the discount are H&M (Beauty and Move included), COS, Weekday, Monki, H&M HOME, & Other Stories, ARKET. In addition to our staff discount, all our employees are included in our H&M Incentive Program – HIP. You can read more about our H&M Incentive Program here. 
In addition to our global benefits, all our local markets offer different competitive perks and benefits. Please note that they may differ between employment type and countries. 
JOIN US​ 
Our uniqueness comes from a combination of many things – our inclusive and collaborative culture, our strong values, and opportunities for growth. But most of all, it’s our people who make us who we are.​ 
​Take the next step in your career together with us. The journey starts here.​ 
​ *We are committed to a recruitment process that is fair, equitable, and based on competency. We therefore kindly ask you to not attach a cover letter in your application.​

jobs.description: Job ID: 7501(Senior) Quantitative Analyst, Model Monitoring and Performance (permanent position)Are you a quantitative analyst with a knack for navigating complex databases and producing clear analysis? Do you have knowledge of credit risk processes and an interest in, or experience with, IRB, IFRS9 or similar models? Then this opportunity may be for you! Quantitative Analyst to join the Model Monitoring and Performance team (MMP) within Risk Models.Nordea are currently developing and implementing a suite of new, state-of-the-art IRB and IFRS9 models. MMP is responsible for ensuring that the new models’ performance is continuously scrutinized, and for identifying any issues arising within them. Further, we are responsible for assessing and overseeing how IRB models are used in credit processes, including whether model use is in line with regulations, internal requirements and the approved purpose of the models.Our key stakeholders are model developers, model users in Business and senior management. About our teamMeet the Model Monitoring and Performance team. Our role is to contribute to assessments of how IRB models are used in credit processes, communicate identified issues and help develop clear internal guidelines for appropriate model use.Our team is an inspiring, competent and creative group of professionals in an international environment. In your daily job, you’ll be applying your quantitative and data analysis skills to produce clear and concise communication about model performance and performance issues to model developers and senior management. You’ll mainly be working with Python, SQL and Snowflake, but SAS and other tools may be used here and there. The role will be located in Helsinki or Stockholm and team colleagues are in Stockholm, Helsinki and Copenhagen.Collaboration. Ownership. Passion. Courage. These are the values that guide us in how we work and how we make decisions – and that we imagine you share with us. What you’ll be doingMain responsibilities in this role:    Quantitative analysis of model performance for all components of IRB and/or IFRS9 models (PD, LGD, EAD).    Communicating conclusions of your analysis to model developers and senior management – in reports and meetings.    Developing, maintaining and operating the IRB and IFRS9 model performance monitoring frameworks.    Collaborating with a variety of stakeholders including risk management, model development, model validation and model users across the bank.    Assessing how IRB models are used in credit processes, identifying potential gaps against regulatory and internal requirements, and communicating conclusions and follow-up needs.Who you areThis is the right role for you if you:    Are driven by a desire to know more.    Love to make sense of data.    Are self-driven and take ownership.    Find it easy to understand others, and make yourself understood by others.    Love to think in terms of the big picture, but know that the devil is in the details.    Enjoy learning, and are excited about bringing your ideas to the table.    Are honest and reliable, and willing to speak up even when it’s difficult.    Think it is important to get governance right.Your background and skills include:    Master’s in a quantitative field such as mathematics, engineering, econometrics, data science, finance, or similar.    Excellent communication skills (English is the working language).    Sound knowledge of applied mathematical modelling and excellent quantitative skills.    Proficiency in Python and SQL.    Knowledge of credit risk processes and how risk models and parameters are used in credit assessment and decision-making.    Knowledge of or interest in IRB, IFRS9 or similar models – practical experience with model use, monitoring or governance is a definitive plus.What we offerPeople come here when they want to get somewhere. For some, it’s to take their career to the next level. For others, it’s to break new ground within their area of expertise – in other words, with us, you will always move forward.A culture that fosters performance and growth in one of the largest Nordic banks, offering various opportunities to evolve, develop and learn from brilliant colleagues with diverse backgrounds in a vibrant working environment.Diversity and inclusion are a natural part of our daily work. We know that an inclusive workplace is a sustainable one. We genuinely believe that our diverse backgrounds, experiences, characteristics and traits make us stronger together. Every day we strive to find new ways to improve diversity and inclusion within our community e.g. we have signed the European Diversity Charters in the countries where we operate to show our commitment and engage with others to continue learning and improving.If this sounds like you, get in touch!Next stepsSubmit your application no later than 03/12/2026.For more information, you’re welcome to contact Rene Eriksen at rene.eriksen@nordea.com.We enable dreams and aspirations for a greater good.We build relationships. We add a personal touch to everything we do – when advising our customers, collaborating with colleagues, and meeting our potential candidates.We learn and develop. We take pride in being experts and thinking ahead. We use our expertise to meet our customers’ needs, from the simplest to the most complex. We bring a growth mindset to our work that enables us to focus on a broader perspective in our daily challenges.We lead change. We are responsible and aware of the impact of our decisions, both for our customers and for our local and global communities. Mindful of our responsibility towards current and future generations, we have made sustainability an integrated part of our business strategy.We are Nordea. We have a 200-year history of supporting and growing the Nordic economies and our values are deeply rooted in these open, progressive and collaborative societies. As one of the biggest employers in the Nordics, Poland and Estonia, you have excellent opportunities to evolve, develop and move forward with us.If you are an external consultant interested in this role and wish to apply please contact the hiring people leader for separate instruction on how to apply.Only for candidates in Sweden: For union information, please contact Finansförbundet at finansforbundet@nordea.se or SACO at SacoNordea@nordea.com.

Company description:Who are we?Volvo Cars is a company on a mission; to bring traditional car manufacturing into a connected, sustainable and smart future.Since 1927, we have been a brand known for our commitment to safety, creating innovative cars that make life less complicated for our consumers. In 2010, we decided to transform our business, resulting in a totally new generation of cars and technologies, as well as steady growth and record sales. Today, we’re expanding our global footprint in Europe, China and the US, and we’re on the lookout for new talent. We are constantly pushing our own skills and abilities to drive change in the automobile industry like never before. We are looking for innovative, committed people to join us in this endeavour and create safe, sustainable and connected cars. We believe in the power of people and will challenge and support you to reach your full potential. Join us and be part of Volvo Cars’ journey into the future.Job description:   Join Lynk & Co Europe, powered by Volvo Cars’ commercial network   Lynk & Co is entering an exciting new phase in Europe. From January 2027, Volvo Cars will become its exclusive European distributor, creating a new commercial set-up that combines Volvo Cars’ established infrastructure with Lynk & Co’s bold and distinctive brand. Employed by Volvo Cars and working closely with Lynk & Co, you’ll have the opportunity to help build this new chapter from the ground up and contribute to the brand’s continued growth across Europe.     What you'll do   As a Warranty Specialist, you will be part of the Warranty team within Aftersales, supporting our European workshop and retailer network. You will play a key role in our daily warranty operations by assessing warranty claims, supporting workshops and retailers, and ensuring that warranty decisions are accurate, consistent and aligned with applicable warranty policies and technical requirements. The role combines technical and financial claim assessment with workshop support, warranty cost control, data analysis and the recovery of eligible warranty costs from manufacturing plants, suppliers and other responsible parties. You will also contribute to the continuous improvement of warranty processes, claim quality and workshop support across European operations. •    Review and assess warranty claims submitted by workshops and make decisions within delegated authority.•    Verify claim eligibility, technical diagnosis, repair information, labour operations, parts usage, costs and supporting documentation.•    Use Lynk & Co technical information and relevant systems, including Codiac, to support consistent and evidence-based warranty decisions.•    Assess whether repairs and parts replacements are technically justified and appropriately documented.•    Provide clear and constructive guidance to workshops and retailers on warranty requirements, claim corrections and required documentation.•    Identify recurring claim-quality issues, unusual cost patterns and potential product-quality concerns.•    Prepare and follow up cases for warranty cost recovery from manufacturing plants, suppliers and other responsible parties.•    Coordinate warranty-related parts returns and provide relevant warranty information to Quality and other stakeholders.•    Analyse claim trends, cost deviations and workshop patterns, and contribute to warranty reporting and KPI follow-up.•    Maintain accurate and traceable warranty documentation and contribute to audits where required.•    Contribute to continuous improvements in warranty processes, working methods and workshop guidance.   Success in the role is measured through the quality, consistency and efficiency of warranty claim handling, timely workshop support, accurate documentation, effective warranty cost control, successful recovery of eligible warranty costs and contribution to the continuous improvement of Warranty operations.     What you'll bring   •    Relevant experience in automotive warranty, aftersales, technical support, claims handling or a comparable field.•    Good understanding of automotive repair processes and workshop operations.•    Ability to accurately assess technical and financial information.•    Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.•    Ability to interpret warranty policies, procedures and technical documentation.•    Good digital skills and confidence working across multiple systems.•    Good written and verbal communication skills in English.•    Ability to manage multiple cases and priorities effectively.•    Ability to make objective, consistent and well-documented decisions.•    Ability to work both independently and collaboratively as part of a team. Experience in one or more of the following areas would be an advantage:•    Automotive manufacturer, importer, national sales company or authorised workshop network.•    Automotive warranty or claim-management systems.•    Codiac or comparable automotive technical and support systems.•    Workshop support, warranty cost recovery or warranty data analysis.•    Microsoft Power BI or similar reporting and analytics tools.

It combines legal expertise, policy research and strategic communication, and suits someone who can explain complex IP and technical topics clearly and engagingly. Company description:At NKT in Karlskrona, we develop and manufacture high voltage power cables that enable the transition to renewable energy. Here, you will be part of an international engineering centre with advanced high voltage test halls, modern cable production and the cable laying vessel NKT Victoria. As Connectors, we collaborate to develop innovative technology that connects a greener and more sustainable world. NKT is headquartered in Denmark and operates in more than 30 countries.NKT - We connect a greener world. www.NKT.com.Job description:Shape competitive high-voltage cable solutions for the energy transitionDo you want to take technical ownership of complex tenders and help shape high-voltage cable systems that enable the transition to renewable energy? As a Tender Lead Engineer at NKT, you will translate customer requirements and tender strategy into compliant and executable HVAC and HVDC cable system solutions. You will combine advanced engineering with technical leadership and customer interaction, working across disciplines and functions in an international environment. This is an opportunity to support key technical decisions at an early stage, contribute directly to NKT’s business growth and work with critical power infrastructure supporting the expansion and interconnection of power grids. Acting as the technical focal point, you will coordinate multidisciplinary engineering activities and ensure the proposed cable system balances technical performance, manufacturability, installation constraints, qualification, risk, cost and schedule. Key responsibilities include:•    Coordinate the complete technical scope and engineering activities of assigned tenders•    Develop and optimize HVAC and HVDC cable system solutions•    Translate requirements and standards into design premises and engineering deliverables•    Manage technical risks, deviations, qualifications and opportunities•    Lead technical customer dialogues, clarifications and negotiations The position is primarily based in Karlskrona but Malmö, Västerås or Rotterdam may also be considered. Regular collaboration across NKT locations is expected, with travel for customer meetings, internal collaboration and tender activities when required. A technical leader with a commercial mindsetYou thrive in a complex technical environment where ownership, structure and collaboration are key. You communicate clearly, build trust and stay focused when priorities shift. You are comfortable working across teams and locations, and you enjoy bringing people together to reach clear decisions. In addition, we believe you bring:•    M.Sc. or Ph.D. in electrical engineering or another relevant engineering discipline, or equivalent technical experience•    Relevant experience in tender engineering, project engineering, cable system design, power transmission or a comparable technically complex industry•    Demonstrated ability to manage and coordinate multidisciplinary technical work with responsibility for scope, quality and deadlines•    Demonstrated capability in requirement analysis, technical documentation and structured risk-based decision-making•    Fluency in spoken and written English•    Experience with high-voltage cable systems, relevant standards, qualification or installation interfaces is an advantage Lead engineering for tomorrow’s energy infrastructureNKT is committed to fostering a diverse organization and a culture where people from different backgrounds can thrive and are inspired to perform at their best. We believe that a diverse organization enables sustainable performance, and that an inclusive and welcoming culture makes for a better place to work. At NKT, you will work at the intersection of engineering, customer needs and commercial strategy, gaining broad exposure to high-voltage cable systems and international tender projects. You will collaborate with specialists across engineering and other functions while developing both your technical leadership and commercial understanding. Your work will contribute directly to cable solutions that support renewable energy integration, power grid expansion and the electrification of society. Read more about our offer and listen to some voices of NKT Connectors here! We will review applications continuously, but we recommend you apply no later than 2026-12-21. The OpportunityWe are seeking a highly skilled and motivated FPGA Developer to join our MACH R&D team at Hitachi Energy Sweden AB. As part of the team developing the industry-leading MACH™ control and protection platform for HVDC systems, you will design, implement, and verify FPGA-based solutions for real-time control, communication, data acquisition, and protection applications. Your work will play a key role in enabling the integration of renewable energy, strengthening power grids, and supporting the global energy transition.How you’ll make an impact    Design, implement, and verify FPGA solutions for real-time control, data acquisition, communication, and signal processing in power quality and HVDC systems.    Develop high-quality VHDL/Verilog RTL code, simulation environments, and verification testbenches to ensure reliable and robust designs.    Collaborate with system architects, software developers, electronics engineers, and product teams to define requirements and deliver integrated solutions.    Perform FPGA bring-up, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing, system integration, validation, and debugging throughout the development lifecycle.    Optimize FPGA designs for performance, timing closure, resource utilization, power consumption, and maintainability. At Sandvik Rock Tools in Sandviken, we're exploring how industrial sensor data can provide earlier and more reliable insight into machine conditions. This thesis combines practical measurements on production equipment with signal processing, data analysis, and AI to establish a reusable approach for future condition-monitoring initiatives. Background and purpose Modern production equipment generates many signals, but existing machine data is not always reliable or sampled at the frequency required for condition assessment. Additional sensors may be needed to capture vibration, temperature, acoustic, electrical, pressure, or other process-related phenomena.  The purpose of this thesis is to evaluate suitable sensors and data-collection methods, then analyze data from selected equipment using statistical and AI-based methods. The result should support further development of condition monitoring, diagnostics, and data-driven maintenance at Rock Tools. Work description The thesis is carried out as a structured proof of concept. Together with the company supervisor, you refine the scope, machine case, and success criteria. The work is expected to include:     Review relevant research on industrial condition monitoring, sensor selection, signal processing, and AI methods.     Define machine states, operating conditions, potential failure modes, and evaluation criteria.     Evaluate sensors and data-acquisition solutions based on sampling rate, installation, synchronization, robustness, accessibility and cost.     Plan and perform data collection, documenting sensor placement, machine settings and data quality.     Clean, synchronize and analyze time-series data using suitable time, frequency or time-frequency features.     Develop and compare statistical baselines and AI models for classification or anomaly detection.     Validate performance, including false alarms, missed detections, changing operating conditions, explainability and uncertainty.     Recommend sensors, an architecture aligned with the Sandvik Rock Tools Unified Namespace, a modelling approach and next steps. Expected deliverables are a sensor and data-acquisition concept, a quality-checked dataset, reproducible analysis and model code, a comparison of methods and a roadmap for continued development. The objective is a robust proof of concept and reusable method, not a production-ready predictive-maintenance platform.   Your profile We're looking for one or two analytical and hands-on students with an interest in industrial equipment, measurement technology, and data science. You work systematically, document decisions, and connect model results to physical machine behavior. Your background includes:     Ongoing Master’s studies in automation, mechatronics, mechanical or electrical engineering, engineering physics, computer science, industrial data science or a related field.     Experience with Python and data analysis.      An understanding of, or motivation to learn, time-series analysis, signal processing, machine learning and experimental design.       Good communication skills in English; Swedish is advantageous.  Experience with vibration analysis, industrial sensors, OPC UA, MQTT, PLC/CNC data or condition monitoring is advantageous, as is Knowledge of NumPy, pandas, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch or TensorFlow. Our culture At Sandvik, we work with advanced technology and exciting innovations, but our people are the key to our success. We believe diversity and inclusion create stronger results through mutual support, knowledge sharing and different perspectives. Visit our stories hub, LinkedIn or Facebook to get to know us further.  Scope The thesis corresponds to 30 ECTS credits and approximately 20 weeks of full-time work. The start date is agreed with the selected student or students and the university.  The position is based at Rock Tools in Sandviken, Sweden, with access to relevant equipment, data and supervision. Confidentiality, data handling and publication boundaries will be agreed at the start of the project. Contact information For more information, please contact Andreas Nelson, Method Development, at Tools, andreas.nelson@sandvik.comWe’ve already decided on which advertising channels and marketing campaigns we wish to use and respectfully decline any additional contacts in that matter. Application Please submit your application by December 13, 2026. Attach your CV, cover letter and transcript of records. Describe your experience with sensor data, signal processing, machine learning or industrial equipment, and what interests you most about the project. Applications by email are not accepted. Job ID: R0099692. Sandvik is a global, high-tech engineering group providing solutions that enhance productivity, profitability and sustainability in the manufacturing, mining and infrastructure industries. Our offering includes equipment, tools, services and digital solutions for machining, mining, rock excavation, crushing and screening.

jobs.occupation: Software Engineer - Machine Learning or Computer Vision
jobs.description: Volumental is the footwear industry’s leading FitTech™ company, using 3D scanning and machine learning to match people with shoes that truly fit.Our vision is “a world without sizes, where every body fits.” We work with brands such as New Balance, Red Wing, Fleet Feet, and Vivobarefoot across 3,000+ stores in 60 countries, with 60M+ foot scans collected, one of the world’s largest datasets of its kind.Computer vision, machine learning, and AI have always been at the core of our product. Today, we also use AI agents as everyday companions in our work, helping us shorten feedback cycles, deepen our expertise, and explore new areas. We believe the best work comes from people who never stop learning and who care deeply about their craft.Our Products and TeamsWe target businesses and stores selling footwear such as shoes, ski boots and hockey skates, as well as insoles. We develop two related products, each with its own team:    In-store product. We sell a 3D scanner that our business customers put in their physical retail stores and use to scan shoppers' feet. The scanner is controlled by a tablet, which shows the 3D scans and recommends footwear from the store's range.    Online product. We sell 3D scanning and recommendation web components that our business customers integrate into their online store. It allows online shoppers to scan their own feet using their own phone and get size recommendations for the footwear in that online store.We are also exploring new product opportunities, such as 3D scanning beyond feet and footwear. You will start in our Online product team, with the chance to move into other teams over time. Whichever team you are in, you will be part of shaping our current and future products. Algorithm Development at VolumentalBoth of our products are built on top of two core algorithmic systems:    3D foot scanning system. It takes images of a person's feet and reconstructs a 3D model. This involves areas such as camera calibration, image processing, image classification, image segmentation, object detection, parametric 3D models, numerical optimization and machine learning.    Footwear recommendation system. This is based on machine learning and our ever-growing dataset of more than 30 million samples of 3D scans matched with footwear purchases. Given a shopper's unique pair of feet, we predict and recommend what footwear will fit them. This involves areas such as machine learning, probabilistic methods, model fitting, numerical optimization, training, inference, ranking, statistics, data visualization, data cleaning and outlier detection.For both systems, we put a strong emphasis on empirical evaluation and optimization, based on data that we continuously gather from our users. We want to measure what works and what does not (yet) work in practice, and find ways to improve it.You will have the chance to work on either of these systems, depending partly on your previous experience and interests and partly on the current needs of our products and users.Our algorithmic tech stack includes technologies like: Python, C++, Go, SQL, NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, Polars, TensorFlow, Keras, JAX, Eigen, Ceres, OpenCV, Google Cloud Platform, BigQuery, Devin AI, Greptile, Claude… You will influence which tools we use, and if you find something better, we want to hear about it. We offer premium AI agent subscriptions and encourage everyone to explore, test, and share useful ways of working with AI. We are excited about you because you:    Have experience in both mathematical modeling and programming.    Are a collaborative and kind team member.    Can solve difficult problems in practice.    Have experience working with datasets and evaluating different methods.    Have a master's degree in computer science, engineering physics, electrical engineering, or similar.It is a plus if you:    Have professional experience of software engineering.    Have professional experience working with algorithms in areas like:    Machine learning    Computer vision    Computer graphics    Image processing    Robotics    Numerical optimization What we can offer you:    Personal learning budget and access to coaching    Opportunity to work with a great team of 15+ nationalities in our English-speaking office    Occupational pension at ITP1 level    Flexible Public Holidays Policy    Options Program    Parental pay top-up    Wellness allowance    Flexible work policy (at least 3 days a week from our Stockholm office) The monthly compensation range for this role in Stockholm is 50,000-77,000 SEK. Actual compensation will depend on level, experience, and skillset as assessed in the interview process.We are hiring for multiple positions and welcome both junior and senior engineers from all backgrounds. We’d love to hear from you!

jobs.occupation: Associate researcher in Experimental lung transplantation
jobs.description: Description of workplaceThe research group is led by Associated professor Sandra Lindstedt and has a long-standing interest in research related to lung transplantation, post-transplant complications, and lung regeneration. The group focuses on developing novel therapeutic strategies to treat lung injury, improve donor organ quality, and reduce complications following lung transplantation. A particular focus is on acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), primary graft dysfunction (PGD), and regenerative approaches to lung repair.We offerLund University is a governmental authority, which means you get special benefits, generous holidays, and a favorable occupational pension. Read more on the university's website about being employed at Lund University, Work at Lund UniversityWork descriptionA associate researcher position is available within the Lindstedt research group, focusing on translational research in lung transplantation, lung injury, and regenerative medicine. The duties at the research unit primarily consist of experimental and laboratory-based research, with a particular focus on the development and evaluation of novel therapeutic strategies to improve lung repair and transplantation outcomes.The main responsibilities include:    independently designing, planning, coordinating, and conducting research projects, as well as collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and managing experimental data.    The work involves the development and optimization of experimental protocols, evaluation of therapeutic interventions, and application of cellular, molecular, ultra-high-plexed immunofluorescence and histological techniques to investigate mechanisms of lung injury, repair, and regeneration.    The position also includes responsibility for preparing high-quality scientific manuscripts for publication in international peer-reviewed journals, contributing to research grant applications, and presenting research findings at national and international scientific conferences.    The majority of the work will be conducted independently, while also involving close collaboration with internal and external research partners and clinical collaborators.    In addition, the position includes mentorship and supervision of doctoral students, Bachelor’s and Master’s students, and other junior researchers, as well as contributing to the coordination and development of ongoing research activities within the group.Other work tasks might also be included.QualificationsRequired qualifications    PhD (or equivalent) in biomedical sciences, biotechnology, molecular biology, regenerative medicine, or a related field.    A minimum of four years of documented research experience following completion of the PhD, demonstrating scientific independence and responsibility.    Documented experience in experimental and translational biomedical research, particularly within cell therapies, lung injury, lung transplantation, or regenerative medicine.    Hands-on experience with small and large-animal models and/or ex vivo organ perfusion.    Experience with standard cellular and molecular biology techniques, including cell culture, ELISA, Western blotting, qPCR, immunohistochemistry and high-plexed immunofluorescence.    Demonstrated ability to independently design, plan, coordinate, and conduct complex experimental research projects.    Documented scientific productivity through publications in international peer-reviewed journals.    Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.    Independent and responsible, with the ability to organize and manage research activities and take responsibility for scientific quality and project progress.    Collaborative, with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively in interdisciplinary research environments.    Analytical and solution-oriented, with the ability to critically evaluate experimental results and address complex scientific challenges.Meritorious qualifications:    Additional specialized training in experimental transplantation, regenerative medicine, cell therapy, or related disciplines.    Relevant training and certification in laboratory animal science, particularly involving large- and small-animal experimental models.    Completed courses in higher education teaching and pedagogy.    Experience with experimental lung transplantation, including large- and small-animal models of lung injury and transplantation.    Hands-on experience with ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP) and human ex vivo lung models, including precision-cut lung slices (PCLS). Department of Biosystems and TechnologyPhD Project: Valorization and Risk Assessment of Anaerobic Digestates for Sustainable Horticultural ProductionThird-cycle subject area: Horticultural ScienceDescription of the doctoral project The transition to circular food and energy systems requires safe, high-quality products that can return nutrients and organic matter to horticultural production. Anaerobic digestate from biogas production is a promising resource containing plant nutrients and organic fibre originating from, for example, manure, food and household waste, slaughterhouse by-products, park and garden residues, and biomass from intermediate crops or roadside vegetation. The digestate can be separated into a nutrient-rich liquid fraction and a fibre fraction. While the liquid fraction has potential for use in nutrient solutions, the fibre fraction is particularly relevant as a constituent of growing media and a potential partial replacement for peat and other fibre materials. Developing safe, functional and locally available alternatives to peat is an important challenge for sustainable horticultural production. A key barrier is the possible presence of pyralid herbicide residues. These herbicides can accumulate in crop material, persist during anaerobic digestion and cause growth disturbances in sensitive horticultural crops at very low concentrations. The project will investigate the occurrence and fate of pyralids in selected feedstocks and digestate fractions, with particular focus on the fibre fraction and its use in growing media.About the positionThe doctoral project will combine greenhouse and growth-chamber bioassays with laboratory studies and chemical characterisation. It will assess effects on plant growth and nutrient uptake, examine the distribution, degradation and immobilisation of herbicide residues, and generate knowledge to support risk assessment and the safe valorisation of digestate-derived growing-media products. The project is an important part in the ongoing transition for more circular productions systems where plant nutrients and fiber is recycled from waste to production. The project is a part of the Biogas Solutions Research Center, which means that there will be collaboration with other PhD students both at SLU and at Linköping University. Communication of results, both orally and in writing to both academic and industrial stakeholders are also important parts of the project. As a PhD-student, you will also take PhD courses and be a part of the daily work at the department.RequirementsTo meet the general entry requirements you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master’s) qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39).Specific entry requirements for the third-cycle courses and study programme in Horticultural Science. To meet the specific entry requirements the applicant must have the equivalent knowledge to a minimum of 90 credits in relevant subject areas. This must include a degree project, and at least 30 credits must be at the advanced level.You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6.You should have received a degree at advanced level (second cycle) within the fields of Horticultural Science, Agricultural Science, or similar subject. You should also have documented experience with laboratory work and experimental work within the field of study.Beneficial competences Driver’s licence valid in Sweden. Documented experience from scientific writing and scientific communication.Your profileWe are looking for an engaged and self-going candidate with genuine interest in horticulture and circular solutions. Suitable backgrounds are as a Horticulturist or Agronomist. Experience with laboratory work, for example microbial analyses, is beneficial. You should also have experience with practical plant cultivation. Great emphasis will be put on personal skills like curiosity, ability to work individually and in group, and ability to independently plan and perform research related tasks. You are expected to be open to new challenges and to take on various work tasks to contribute to the development of the department’s activities. Very good skills in speaking and writing in English is mandatory.About usAt the department of Biosystems and Technology you will work in a multi-disciplinary environment together with around 60 colleagues, among which around 10 PhD students. The holder of this position will be a part of a national, transdisciplinary center of excellence called Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC). Here, new and relevant knowledge is generated through collaboration between different scientific disciplines as well as between researchers and practitioners from industry and public organizations. The BSRC includes researchers and support from two universities (Linköping University and SLU) and about 50 private and public organizations involving all parts of the biogas system and has additional support from Swedish Energy Agency. All doctoral positions advertised within BSRC will be formulated so that they fit into the competence center's research plans and at the same time reflect our parties' interests. This way, we ensure long-term competence supply to both industry and academia.Read more about third-cycle courses and study programmes on http://www.slu.se/utbildning/program-kurser/forskarutbildning/Form of employment / Funding Employment as a doctoral student (4-year programme). jobs.description: Department of Biosystems and TechnologyPhD project: Sustainable utilisation of agricultural green biomass in integrated protein and biogas systemsSubject area: TechnologyDescription of the doctoral project A circular and fossil-independent bioeconomy requires renewable biomass without increasing competition for agricultural land and food production. Crop residues and intermediate crops are therefore particularly relevant resources. Research at SLU shows that these biomass resources can be substantial, but their potential and sustainable utilisation vary regionally. They can be used for biogas, while effects on soil carbon and nutrient cycling need to be considered.  Green biomass can also be biorefined into plant protein for feed or food, after which the remaining streams are used for biogas. The same feedstock can thereby provide protein, energy and recycled nutrients.The project aims to assess the potential and consequences of large-scale utilisation of green crop residues and intermediate crops in integrated biogas and green biorefinery systems.The project will:    assess sustainably available biomass from green crop residues and intermediate crops in Sweden;    assess the potential for biogas and combined plant protein and biogas production;    develop implementation scenarios based on feedstock availability, infrastructure, logistics and markets;    assess effects on nutrient cycling, soil carbon, biomethane, fertilizer use, and feed and food production; and    evaluate economic and wider socio-economic benefits, drawbacks and trade-offs.The project combines GIS and agricultural data with mass and nutrient balances, scenario modelling, and life cycle-based, techno-economic and socio-economic methods. Data will be drawn from research, statistics, literature and national databases.The doctoral student will join an interdisciplinary research environment at SLU Alnarp focusing on sustainable agricultural production, bioenergy, circular bioeconomy and systems analysis.About the positionThe work includes collection and processing of agricultural and process data, GIS, modelling of biomass and product flows, scenario development, and environmental and economic assessments.  You will integrate information from crop production and biomass availability to biorefineries, biogas, and food and energy systems.  You will analyse data, develop models and scenarios, and publish and present research results. The work will be conducted with researchers at SLU and external partners.  The doctoral student will be part of the Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC), a national transdisciplinary centre where Linköping University, SLU and around 50 private and public organisations collaborate. The centre is supported by the Swedish Energy Agency. The PhD project follows BSRC’s research plans and contributes to long-term competence development in industry and academia.RequirementsTo meet the general entry requirements you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master’s) qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39).Specific entry requirements for the third-cycle courses and study programme in technology. You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6.You should have a Master’s degree or equivalent in, for example, biosystems/agricultural engineering, environmental engineering, agricultural science, energy systems, industrial ecology, environmental science or a related field.Your profileWe are looking for a motivated candidate interested in sustainable agricultural and bioeconomy systems and quantitative analysis.Experience or documented knowledge in one or several of the following areas is desirable:    systems analysis, modelling or scenario analysis;    GIS and spatial analysis;    life cycle assessment, environmental systems analysis or material-flow analysis;    techno-economic or socio-economic assessment;    bioenergy, biogas or biorefinery systems;    agricultural production systems and agricultural biomass;    statistical analysis and handling of larger datasets;    experience of programming or quantitative modelling, for example using Python, R or MATLAB.You should have good analytical skills, be able to integrate information from different fields, work independently and collaborate well.Excellent written and spoken English is required. Knowledge of Swedish is advantageous but not required.Personal qualities, motivation and the ability to successfully complete doctoral studies will be given considerable weight.
