We have the power of over 50,000 students and co-workers. Students who provide hope for the future. Co-workers who contribute to Linköping University meeting challenges of today. Our fundamental values rest on credibility, trust and security. By having the courage to think freely and innovate, our actions together, large and small, contribute to a better world. We look forward to receiving your application! Are you interested in the potential of citizens' assemblies and other democratic innovations to drive climate transformation? Come join us!Work assignments The Environmental Change division (tema Miljöförändring) at the Department of Thematic Studies is looking to hire a two-year postdoctoral researcher specializing in democratic innovations.You will be part of the Formas-funded research project Democratic Innovations for Climate Transformation (2027-2029), which entails a systematic and interdisciplinary knowledge synthesis of how climate citizens’ assemblies and related democratic processes can contribute to system transformation. The project explores what the existing research literature tells us about the political impact of climate assemblies, how they might contribute to broader systemic transformations, and what this means for Swedish climate governance.As postdoc on the project, you will take a leading role in carrying out the systematic literature review across academic databases and grey literature, following established standards for searching, screening, and quality assessment. You will contribute centrally to the comparative synthesis of findings across studies, and to identifying evidence gaps in how deliberative processes connect to system-level transformation. You will also help design and facilitate stakeholder dialogues with Swedish municipalities and practitioners, which ensures that the resulting knowledge is robust and genuinely useful for policy and practice.You will work in close collaboration with the project’s principal investigator and a research team from LiU and Stockholm Resilience Centre. There is considerable room to help shape the project’s methodological choices and analytical framework, and to co-author academic outputs arising from the review and synthesis work.As postdoc, you will principally carry out research. A certain amount of teaching may be part of your duties, up to a maximum of 20% of working hours.QualificationsTo be qualified to take employment as postdoc, you must have been awarded a doctoral degree or have a foreign degree that is deemed to be equivalent to a doctoral degree. This degree must have been awarded at the latest by the point at which LiU makes its decision to employ you.Your doctoral degree should preferably have been awarded no more than three years ago. If there are special reasons, a degree awarded more than three years ago may be accepted. Special reasons include sick leave, parental leave, trade union positions of trust, service in the defense, or other similar circumstances, as well as service or assignments relevant to the subject area.We are looking for someone with a doctoral degree in social sciences, humanities, or related fields, and a demonstrated familiarity with the research area of democratic innovations – for example, deliberative democracy, citizens’ assemblies, participatory governance, or environmental/climate governance. Experience carrying out systematic literature reviews and others forms of qualitative content analysis is considered a merit. So is prior experience with stakeholder involvement and co-production through workshops and similar formats.You are curious, rigorous, and comfortable moving between the fine-grained work of systematic screening and coding and the bigger-picture task of synthesizing what it all means. You enjoy working collaboratively, taking initiative, and are able to communicate complex research to non-academic audiences, such as policymakers and practitioners. A strong command of written and spoken English is required.The workplaceYou will be employed at the Department of Thematic Studies where you will be affiliated with the Environmental Change theme. You can read about the workplace https://liu.se/en/organisation/liu/tema/temam.The employmentThis employment is a temporary full-time contract of two years. Starting date is Januari 1, 2027, or as soon as possible. Salary and employment benefitsAt Linköping University, salaries are set individually and differentiated, in accordance with the applicable collective agreements (RALS/RALS-T) and the university’s salary-setting guidelines.More information about employee benefits is available https://liu.se/en/work-at-liu/employee-benefits.Union representativesInformation about union representatives, see https://liu.se/en/work-at-liu/hjalp%20for%20sokande.Application procedureApply for the position by clicking the “Apply” button. Your application must be received no later than 27 November, 2026.Applications and documents received after the date above will not be considered. Please attach your selected research publications electronically, in pdf or word format, in the application template. Research publications, e.g. monographs, which cannot be sent electronically should be sent in three sets by mail to the University Registrar at Linköping University, University Registrar, S-581 83 Linköping, Sweden. The publications must be received by Linköping University no later than the deadline for application. Please note that printed publications will not be returned. They will be archived at Linköping University. In the event of a discrepancy between the English translation of the job announcement and the Swedish original, the Swedish version shall take precedent. We welcome applicants with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives - diversity enriches our work and helps us grow. Preserving everybody's equal value, rights and opportunities is a natural part of who we are. Read more about our work with: https://liu.se/en/article/lika-villkor/.We look forward to receiving your application! jobs.occupation: Technical Procurement Manager– Utility-scale solar and BESS
jobs.description: Do you want to lead procurement for the construction of the largest solar and battery storage projects in the Nordics? We are looking for a skilled procurement professional with a strong commercial foundation and the curiosity to understand technical solutions in depth. You are willing to dig into specifications, ask questions and work closely with engineers and suppliers to make well-informed purchasing decisions in a rapidly evolving industry. Join us and be part of an ambitious team building the energy infrastructure of tomorrow.What will you do at NYAB? As our Technical Procurement Manager, you will work at the intersection of long-term sourcing strategy and practical project delivery, leading procurement for utility-scale solar and battery energy storage system (BESS) projects. Your scope will include core components and services such as solar modules, inverters, mounting systems, transformers, batteries, subcontractors and related technical solutions. In this role, you will:     Own and develop the end-to-end procurement lifecycle, from early tendering and supplier evaluation to contracting and execution.     Lead strategic and commercial negotiations to secure competitive terms, balanced risk positions and strong contractual outcomes.     Evaluate supplier offers against technical requirements, cost, quality and delivery needs, working with engineering colleagues to clarify specifications and understand trade-offs.    Stay ahead of the market by identifying new technologies, suppliers and system solutions that strengthen our renewable energy projects and make our supply chain more resilient    Drive procurement priorities against project requirements, schedules and budgets – and make sure we deliver. You will act as our internal product owner, digging into specifications, drawings and technical documentation together with the engineering team until you know the product as well as the supplier does. About you You are a goal-oriented self-starter with the persistence to follow through and make things happen. You combine sound commercial judgment with technical curiosity and a willingness to work through details, ask questions and understand what you are buying. You remain composed during complex contractual discussions and take ownership of your commitments, combining speed with precision and going the extra mile when it matters. Along the way, you build trust with colleagues, suppliers and partners.We believe you have:     A master’s degree in engineering, preferably within electrical engineering, mechanical engineering or energy systems.     At least three years of hands-on experience in large-scale procurement projects with complex technical scopes, ideally in an EPC environment.     Experience in end-to-end sourcing, supplier management and commercial or contractual negotiations.     Strong cost awareness and the ability to manage priorities within time and budget constraints.     Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.     The willingness to travel internationally to meet suppliers and partners, and to visit project sites in Sweden and abroad. It is an advantage if you have:     Experience in construction, electrical systems, renewable energy or another technically complex project environment.     Experience procuring equipment or services for solar parks, BESS or related energy infrastructure.     Excellent written and verbal communication skills in Swedish.Why work at NYAB? NYAB's greatest strength is our drive and the pride we take in our work. We all pull in the same direction – forward. We value people for their competence and initiative, and you get the freedom to act along with the accountability that comes with it. Our entrepreneurial spirit is built on collaboration and commitment. We are a close-knit community where colleagues support one another, share knowledge and work together to find solutions when new challenges arise. You will never work alone – you will have the support of colleagues and leaders, and plenty of room to grow. We also offer:    Comprehensive health assessments     Generous wellness allowance     Parental pay supplement    Reduced working hours – (Sw: arbetstidsförkortning)    A secure pension planReady to make it happen? Apply with your CV or LinkedIn profile. We review applications on an ongoing basis and look forward to hearing from you. Start: As agreed   Employment type: Full-time   Location: Hägersten, Stockholm

jobs.employer_name: Who Collaborating Centre For Int Drug Monitoring
jobs.description: Would you like to contribute to safer use of medicines and vaccines globally? We are looking for a Data Scientist for the Research Department at Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC). You will join a multicultural and dynamic environment with a clear focus to ensure patient safety globally.Since 1978, Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC) has been dedicated to developing, supporting, and expanding the field of pharmacovigilance science and practice.As a World Health Organization (WHO) Collaborating Centre, we support work around the world to examine the potential adverse effects of medicines and vaccines and contribute to safer, more informed care of patients.We are a diverse, international group of pharmacists, physicians, data scientists, system developers, communicators, and many other professionals motivated by a deep belief that the work we do matters.About the roleResearch at UMC is a team effort. Pharmacovigilance experts, engineers, and data scientists work side by side to develop the best ideas and solutions. We are looking for a Data Scientist with excellent technical skills who thrives on collaboration. You will join a self-organising agile team where members share ideas openly, plan their work together, give each other honest feedback, and take joint ownership of outcomes.You will report to our Head of Data Science, Angnis Schmidt-May.What you will do You will help us make better use of data from different sources, the main one being our global database of adverse event reports. Your work will mostly cover the following areas:    Machine learning, natural language processing & large language models: develop methods to support signal management using data from case reports and scientific literature. You will judge carefully when and how AI can be trusted to enhance our research.    Scientific research and dissemination: design and run studies in internal and external collaborations, publish in peer-reviewed journals and present at international conferences.    Sharing methods and assets: make our methods and tools available to others, for example as open-source packages, documented workflows, and reusable models.    Product research: develop innovative methods and conduct exploratory research to improve UMC's products and services. You will work closely with product teams to turn research ideas into useful product features.Who you are    You are an excellent collaborator. You listen to others and build on their ideas. You share credit and lift the people around you.    You are curious and eager to grow. You seek feedback, reflect on it and act on it. You see learning and development as a lifelong part of your career.    You care about the purpose. Patient safety matters to you, and you hold yourself to high standards of scientific integrity. Must have    PhD in a quantitative field (e.g., statistics, computer science, computational linguistics, epidemiology, physics), or a master's degree and PhD-equivalent research experience    Track record of scientific work, such as peer-reviewed publications or conference presentations    Minimum of 5 years of practical experience in data science (from industry or research)    Strong Python/R skills    Fluent written and spoken EnglishNice to haveKnowledge of    best practices in software engineering    pharmacovigilance, medical terminologies (e.g., MedDRA) or experience working with health dataExperience    working on open-source code    working with cloud infrastructure    working with GenAI and agentic workflows    taking models and methods from research into production    working with user research and product development    mentoring or supervising othersUppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC) is an independent, self-funded, non-profit foundation established in 1978 dedicated to safer use of medicines and vaccines. Through an agreement between the Government of Sweden and the World Health Organization (WHO), UMC operates the Programme for International Drug Monitoring, supporting over 180 member countries and regions in strengthening safety surveillance, and maintains VigiBase, the WHO global database of adverse event reports. In addition, UMC provides international standards and related digital solutions for secure exchange of pharmacovigilance data, including a global medicine and vaccine terminology for identification of medicinal products. With around 200 staff, UMC advances the science of pharmacovigilance and transforms its practice through technological innovation.UMC’s working language is English. We normally apply a probationary period to new appointments.If you have any questions regarding this position please contact the responsible manager. You will find the contact details at the end of this page.UMC follows the collective agreements between the Swedish Agency for Government Employers and Saco-S and ST. Union representatives are Malin Zaar (Saco-S) and Jessica Avasol (ST), +46 (0)18-65 60 60.

We are looking for a researcher in Psychology for a fixed-term position at the School of Behavioral, Social and Legal Sciences (BSR). The research is within the area of cognitive neuroscience of aging.Subject areaThe subject area for this position is Psychology.BackgroundThe Division of Psychology at Örebro University is part of the School of Behavioural, Social and Legal Sciences (BSR), together with the Divisions of Legal Science, Criminology, and Social Work.Örebro university is now hiring a researcher within the area of cognitive neuroscience of aging, with a particular focus on early life predictors of brain structural and functional connectivity in older age. The research will be conducted within the research environment LEADER (Center for Lifespan Developmental Research), which is headed by Jonas Persson, Professor in Psychology.Duties and responsibilitiesThe research duties include preprocessing and analyses of structural and functional brain imaging data obtained by magnetic resonance imaging. A particular focus will be on analysing diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) data to assess structural connectivity and brain network properties in older age and how these related to health, cognition, lifestyle and other factors in childhood and adolescence. Analyses of functional connectivity data from resting-state fMRI images and the relationship with early life predictors is also expected. The applicant will also have a leading role in dissemination of the results through international peer-reviewed publication and presentations.  QualificationsThose qualified for the appointment as a researcher are applicants who have obtained a doctoral degree or have a degree from abroad deemed to correspond to a doctoral degree.Assessment criteriaA general basis for assessment is that the applicant is able to demonstrate the personal qualities required to successfully perform the duties and responsibilities at hand; that they are able to cooperate with other members of staff; and contribute to the development of university operations.Specific personal abilities that are of great importance for the position is documented expertise in the fields of cognitive aging and brain imaging. Of particular importance is proficiency in analysing structural brain connectivity data, connectome-based modelling and tractography of diffusion-tensor imaging (DTI)/DWI data combined with a documented ability in analysing functional MRI data. Experience of working with longitudinal MRI data is also highly desirable, along with experience in working with software such as Matlab, R and SPM.InformationThis is a fixed-term full-time position for 12 months. At Örebro University, salary depends on the successful candidate’s qualifications and experience.For more information about the position, contact Jonas Persson +46 19 301428, email: jonas.persson@oru.se, or Head of Unit Terese Glatz, +46 19 301205, email: terese.glatz@oru.se.At Örebro University, we expect each member of staff to be open to development and change; take responsibility for their work and performance; demonstrate a keen interest in collaboration and contribute to development; as well as to show respect for others by adopting a constructive and professional approach.Örebro University actively pursues equal opportunities and gender equality as well as a work environment characterised by openness, trust and respect. We value the qualities that diversity adds to our operations.ApplicationThe application is made online. Click the button “Apply” to begin the application procedure.For the application to be complete, the following electronic documents must be included:    Covering letter, outlining how you believe you can contribute to the continued development of Örebro University    CV with a relevant description of your overall qualifications and experience    Account of research qualifications and experience    Copies of relevant course/degree certificates and references verifying eligibility and criteria metOnly documents written in Swedish, English, Norwegian and Danish can be reviewed. More information for applicants will be found on our career site:  https://www.oru.se/english/career/available-positions/applicants-and-external-experts/The application deadline is November 27, 2026. We look forward to receiving your application!As we have already made our choices in terms of external collaboration partners and marketing efforts for this recruitment process, we decline any contact with recruitment agencies and advertisers.As directed by the National Archives of Sweden (Riksarkivet), we are required to deposit one file copy of the application documents, excluding publications, for a period of two years after the appointment decision has gained legal force.

About VolumentalVolumental is a FitTech™ company used by footwear brands and retailers, matching people with shoes that truly fit through 3D scanning and machine learning.Our vision is "a world without sizes, where every body fits". We work with brands like New Balance, Red Wing, Fleet Feet, and Vivobarefoot across 3,000+ stores in 60 countries, with 60M+ foot scans collected, one of the world's largest datasets of its kind.We've always been an AI company at our core. Today, that extends beyond the product into how we build, using AI agents and strong self-serve tooling to move faster from idea to production. Where you fit in  Every scan in every one of those stores, and every recommendation we give, depends on infrastructure that has to work while a shopper is standing in front of a clerk. Our platform runs on Kubernetes on Google Cloud, is managed as code, is deployed through GitOps, and is observed through Grafana. What we’re looking for is someone who treats that platform as a product: one our developers can self-serve on, that holds up when things go wrong, and that is ready for new kinds of workloads.This is a hands-on Platform Engineer role. Most days you'll be shipping and running infrastructure with Terraform, Helm and ArgoCD, keeping an eye on our systems through Grafana, and building tools in Go that let developers get what they need without waiting on anyone. You'll also spend time explaining technical tradeoffs and writing docs that others can act on.AI is changing the industry, and we see it as an opportunity to empower people. By automating toil and mechanical tasks across the organisation, people can focus on the architectural, novel, and creative work. You will be right at the centre of this transformation, enabling not only yourself and your team’s work, but ensuring that the company can leverage AI and accelerate as a whole.Things you'll do:     Ship and run production infrastructure on Kubernetes and GCP, managed as code with Terraform and deployed with Helm and ArgoCD    Define SLOs and build monitoring and alerting in Grafana that tells us when stores and shoppers are actually affected    Take part in on-call, lead incident response, and run postmortems that turn into real fixes    Build tools in Go that let developers self-serve on environments, deployments and access    Explain technical tradeoffs to engineers, product managers and leadership, and write documentation others can act on    Leverage AI agents to compress routine work, redirecting the time saved into reliability and platform improvements    Help strengthen how we handle access, secrets, certificates and image security alongside the wider teamWe are excited about you because:    You have 3+ years of experience running production infrastructure in an SRE, DevOps or Platform role    You've been on-call for production systems on Kubernetes and a major cloud provider, ideally GCP, and have led incident response and postmortems    You can set up SLO-based monitoring and alerting, and you're comfortable managing infrastructure as code with Terraform    You write clean, maintainable, cloud-native code in at least one language such as Go or Python    You have solid systems knowledge and troubleshoot methodically across the stack    You're comfortable with ambiguity and enjoy finding the right problem and seeing it throughBonus - Don't let these stop you from applying, but please let us know if you have experience with:    Deploying and running AI agent workloads and tool servers (such as MCP), with sandboxing, rate limiting and observability of agent actions    Security: identity and access management, authentication (OAuth/OIDC, SSO), certificate and TLS/mTLS management, secrets handling, network hardening, vulnerability management, and image hardening and scanning    Compliance frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2 or GDPR    Database operations and migrations    Running workloads across multiple cloud providers or regulated regions What we can offer you:    Personal learning budget and access to coaching    Opportunity to work with a great team of 20+ nationalities in our English-speaking office    Occupational pension at ITP1 level    Flexible Public Holidays Policy    Options Program    Parental pay top-up    Wellness allowance    Flexible work policy (at least 3 days a week from our Stockholm office) The monthly compensation range for this role in Stockholm is 52,000-66,000 SEK. Actual compensation will depend on level, experience, and skillset as assessed in the interview process.This is a full-time position based at our Stockholm headquarters. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds! If this role excites you but you don't meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply - we'd love to hear from you.Feel free to include a link to your GitHub or anything you've built or operated that you're proud of.How we hireWe use generative AI to assist the people running our recruitment process, for example in preparing interviews. People are in the loop at every stage, and every decision about your application is made by a human.

jobs.occupation: Master Thesis: AI for Real-Time Microstructure Monitoring Using Laser Ultra
jobs.description: Project Description Background Laser Ultrasonics (LUS) is a powerful non-contact technique for in-situ characterization of metallic materials at elevated temperatures. In hot strip mill environments, LUS enables real-time monitoring of grain size evolution through analysis of ultrasonic wave attenuation and velocity, providing critical insight into recrystallization, grain growth, and phase transformations. This information is highly valuable for advanced process control strategies aimed at improving product quality, consistency, and resource efficiency. The NAICE project (Non-destructive AI enhanced online grain size evaluation) addresses a key challenge in fossil free steel production: today’s steel mills lack real time information about the microstructure that governs material quality, leading to unnecessary energy use, scrap, and slow process adjustments. By upgrading the world’s only industrial laser ultrasonic grain size gauge and collecting a unique large dataset, the project will train models to enable AI enhanced measurement of the grain size and microstructure in real-time. This enables smarter process control, higher yield, and reduced emissions. This thesis is the first of two planned master thesis works. The first will evaluate the best options using historical data sets, whereas the second will focus on using the full dataset and optimizing the model for industrial implementation. If you want to know more about the LUS technology and the installation of the world’s only grain size gauge there is a recorded webinar here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZOpXUAPhEv0&t=665s  Thesis Scope The thesis will focus on the application of machine learning and AI techniques to Laser Ultrasonic (LUS) data acquired in a hot strip mill environment. The available dataset consists of:     Raw LUS A-scan signals with multiple backwall echoes (20 µs duration, 1 ns resolution)     Grain size values calculated using an established conventional algorithm (serving as reference values)     The primary objective is to develop and evaluate AI-based approaches for: - Grain size prediction directly from raw laser ultrasonic signals - Microstructure state classification (e.g., recrystallized fraction, pancaking/aspect ratio) A key part of the work will be to survey suitable AI architectures, such as time-series models, deep learning approaches, and alternative signal-processing-informed models, and assess their applicability to the LUS data. Tasks     Survey and critically assess relevant AI/ML architectures for ultrasonic time-series data     Pre-process and structure high-resolution LUS A-scan datasets for model training     Develop and implement selected AI models     Perform benchmark comparisons between different approaches with respect to:      Prediction accuracy     Robustness to signal variability     Computational efficiency and suitability for real-time deployment     Analyze model interpretability in relation to known physical phenomena Expected Outcomes The thesis should deliver:     A structured comparison of candidate AI approaches for LUS-based grain size prediction     Prototype models demonstrating feasibility on the historical dataset     Recommendations for model selection in future industrial implementation Desired Qualifications We are looking for a motivated student with:     A background in computer engineering, engineering physics, materials science, applied mathematics, or similar     Strong interest in machine learning and signal processing     Experience with Python/Matlab and ML frameworks     Basic understanding of wave physics, ultrasonics, or materials science (meriting but not required)     Analytical mindset and ability to work with complex datasets Additional Information     The work will be carried out in close collaboration with experts in Laser Ultrasonics and industrial process monitoring, providing a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge development of AI-driven process control in steel manufacturing. Project time The project is intended for a master thesis (30hp), starting in spring 2027 or can be mutually decided through negotiations. Further information This project is intended to be performed at Swerim in Stockholm. Swerim rewards the student with 50 000 SEK for an approved master thesis (30hp). Contacts For further information please contact:      Mikael Malmström, mikael.malmstrom@swerim.se     Hampus Wikmark Kreuger, hampus.wikmark@swerim.se Application Apply by using the application function below. The application can be written in Swedish (or English). You will receive a confirmation that Swerim has received your application. Please note that we fill the position as soon as we find a suitable applicant, which means there is no explicit deadline.
